summary: Re-grilled after the mechanism pivot. The original hook-based approach was verified infeasible against Claude Code docs (no plan-mode hook fires; #21282), and the human chose the CLI attributed approve mechanism via AskUserQuestion. The spec now describes forge plan approve --by writing the marker, plan save refusing without a fresh body-digest match, and plan mode as the review step not the enforcement signal.
gaps: The original spec asserted a hook writes the marker on ExitPlanMode approval. Verified infeasible: PostToolUse/PreToolUse do not fire for plan-mode transitions (#21282); ExitPlanMode fires only PermissionRequest, a decision-gate before the human decides, which cannot record that the human approved this plan. Resolved: the enforcement is forge plan approve --by (human chat confirmation, decision-accept trust model); plan mode remains the review presentation.
The digest must bind what the human approved to what plan save records. Resolved: both digest the plan BODY (not the machine frontmatter); an edit after approval fails the match and is refused.
resolutions: Mechanism is forge plan approve --by <name>, refused without a human --by, writing the body-digest marker; plan save sets awaiting-approval and refuses approved without a fresh matching marker.
Plan mode is the recommended human-review step (ExitPlanMode), documented as review not enforcement, because Claude Code emits no plan-mode hook to enforce against.
Every existing plan-save gate is preserved; this adds the human gate.
open_items: Decision 0029 carries the dated correction of the hook approach; it stays accepted because the human directed the corrected mechanism.
If Claude Code later adds plan-mode hooks (#21282), a follow-up could bind the marker to the plan-mode approval directly; the CLI command remains the auditable path.
